title: Crypto misuse: GCM streaming encrypt produces ciphertext before tag — plaintext oracle if session abandoned
description:
wolfssl GCM update() callback calls wc_AesGcmEncryptUpdate() and returns ciphertext to caller on each write(). kcapi AEAD buffers all input until finalize() and produces ciphertext+tag atomically.

wolfCrypt analysis (aes.c):
- wc_AesGcmEncryptUpdate() calls AesGcmCryptUpdate_C() which is a CTR-mode XOR loop — encrypts every input byte immediately and writes to out buffer. No plaintext buffering. (lines 12416-12475)
- Sub-block carryover: partial AES block keystream is cached in aes->streamData for next call — this is keystream caching, NOT plaintext buffering.
- wc_AesGcmEncryptFinal() produces ONLY the authentication tag (GHASH finalization). No ciphertext. (lines 12487-12532)

Consequence: caller receives real, correctly-encrypted ciphertext on each write() — but the authentication tag is not available until FINALIZE. A caller who calls write() N times and abandons the session (no FINALIZE) receives N chunks of unauthenticated ciphertext. The ciphertext is not garbage — it is the correct CTR-mode encryption — which makes this more dangerous: the caller may process it without noticing the missing tag.

kcapi provider does not have this problem: it buffers all plaintext internally and produces ciphertext+tag together at finalize().

The two providers have incompatible security models at the UAPI level. Callers cannot safely switch providers without changing session flow.
close_reason: wolfssl GCM encrypt now buffers plaintext in inbuf during update() and calls wc_AesGcmEncrypt() one-shot at finalize(). Ciphertext+tag produced atomically — consistent with kcapi AEAD batch model. Added get_finalize_output_size callback so framework pre-allocates correct outbuf.
